mainTopic: The כהן גדול as an אונן; his practice עבודה before יום הכיפורים; and רבי עקיבא's view that sprinkling makes a pure person impure
overview: This amud opens with רבא finishing his explanation of רבי יהודה. A כהן גדול who is an אונן may serve by Torah law, but the Rabbis decreed that he not serve that whole day, in case he eats קדשים. רב אדא בר אהבה challenges this from יום הכיפורים, where רבי יהודה makes no such decree. רבא answers that on יום הכיפורים nobody eats, so there is no worry. A new משנה then teaches that during the seven days before יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול performs the main daily services to practice, and that all year he has first choice of service and portions. רב חסדא says this משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא, who holds that sprinkling פרה אדומה water on a pure person makes him impure. The גמרא explains how רבי עקיבא and the חכמים each read the verse, and how each understands שלמה's puzzle about פרה אדומה. It then shows that the 'מזה' who must wash his clothes is really someone who carries the water, and that he becomes impure only if he carries a sprinkling's worth of water. A משנה about the amount the vessel must hold begins at the end of the amud and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's decree: a כהן גדול who is an אונן does not serve all day
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes explaining רבי יהודה: a כהן גדול who is an אונן does not serve all day, because of a rabbinic decree that he might eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי יהודה's words come] to say that he does not serve the whole day. This is a decree, in case he eats [קדשים].
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of רבא's explanation of what רבי יהודה meant about a כהן גדול who is an אונן (a mourner on the day a close relative died). רבא says that רבי יהודה does not let him serve for that entire day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law a כהן גדול may do the עבודה even while he is an אונן. But an אונן is forbidden to eat קדשים. So the Rabbis worried that if he keeps serving, he might forget and eat from the offerings, and they made a גזירה that he should not serve that day.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made as a protective fence
Lest he eat (קדשים, which an אונן may not eat)
A mourner on the day a close relative died, before burial

steps.confusionAlert: The ban on serving is NOT from the Torah. The Torah allows a כהן גדול who is an אונן to serve. This is only a rabbinic גזירה, made to protect him from eating קדשים.

phrases.english: To say that he does not serve the entire day,
phrases.notes: Completes רבא's explanation, which began earlier

phrases.english: a decree, lest he eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's answer earlier explaining רבי יהודה's position
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה holds that a כהן גדול who is an אונן does not serve all day, because of a rabbinic decree lest he eat קדשים.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יהודה made no such decree on יום הכיפורים
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה points to רבי יהודה's ruling about preparing a backup wife. There, if the wife dies, the כהן גדול still serves, and no decree is made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: Did רבי יהודה really make a decree in case he eats? But we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה says, they even prepare another wife for him, in case his wife dies. And if his wife dies, he still does the עבודה, and רבי יהודה did not decree in case he eats!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבא by showing that elsewhere רבי יהודה does not seem to worry that the כהן גדול might eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול needs a wife ('וכפר בעדו ובעד ביתו'). So רבי יהודה says to prepare a second wife in case the first one dies. That means if his wife dies on יום הכיפורים, he becomes an אונן and still serves. So רבי יהודה made no decree there, which seems to contradict רבא's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And did he really decree? (opens a challenge)
They prepare another wife for him

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאכַל?
phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yehuda decree lest he eat?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They even prepare another wife for him,
phrases.notes: From the first משנה of the tractate

phrases.english: lest his wife die.
And if his wife dies, he performs the service,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאכַל!
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda did not decree lest he eat!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי גָּזַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה שֶׁמָּא יֹאכַל? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that רבי יהודה decreed an אונן כהן גדול may not serve, lest he eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the יום הכיפורים case, רבי יהודה lets a כהן גדול whose wife died keep serving with no decree. That suggests רבי יהודה does not worry that he will eat.

steps.title: יום הכיפורים is different because nobody eats
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that on יום הכיפורים there is no worry he will eat, since everyone is fasting. On other days everyone eats, so the worry is real.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: How can you compare? There, since it is יום הכיפורים, when nobody eats, he too will not come to eat. Here, when everyone eats, he too will come to eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his explanation by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The decree exists only because the אונן כהן גדול might eat קדשים. On יום הכיפורים the whole world is fasting, so there is no danger and no need for a decree. On a regular day everyone around him is eating, so he could easily forget and eat too.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (the cases are different)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי יהודה decreed that an אונן כהן גדול does not serve on a regular day, lest he eat. On יום הכיפורים no decree is needed, because nobody eats.

phrases.english: He said to him: How can you compare?!
There, since it is Yom Kippur,
when everyone does not eat,
he too will not come to eat;
here, when everyone eats —
he too will come to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה made no decree on יום הכיפורים, he never worries that the כהן גדול might eat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry depends on the setting. On יום הכיפורים nobody eats, so there is no worry and no decree.

steps.title: Challenge: the wife was divorced, so there is no mourning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אנינות could apply at all in the יום הכיפורים case. According to רבי יהודה, the wife was already given a divorce.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in a case like this, does אנינות take effect on him? But she is divorced!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new difficulty from a different angle. In רבי יהודה's case, why would the כהן גדול be an אונן at all?
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the כהן גדול gives one of his two wives a conditional גט, so that he will not have two wives. So if a wife dies, she may count as already divorced, and a man does not become an אונן for a divorced woman. Then רב אדא's comparison falls apart, because there was no אנינות to decree about in the first place.

keyTerms.meaning: The legal status of an אונן

phrases.english: And in a case like this,
does acute mourning take effect on him?
But she is divorced!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הַאי גַּוְונָא מִי חָיְילָא עֲלֵיהּ אֲנִינוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the premise behind the challenge and answer of steps 2 and 3
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the כהן גדול whose wife died on יום הכיפורים is an אונן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה requires a conditional divorce. A divorced woman's death does not create אנינות, so there is nothing to compare.

steps.title: He is still emotionally troubled
steps.stepSummary: Even if formal אנינות does not apply, he is still upset by her death. So the case is still a fair comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted that אנינות does not take effect on him, but is he not troubled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that even without the legal status of an אונן, the כהן גדול is still distressed and distracted by his wife's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the comparison is not the formal label of אנינות. It is that the כהן גדול is grieving and distracted, which could make him forget himself. So the case still fits, and רבא's answer about יום הכיפורים still explains why no decree was made there.

phrases.english: Granted that acute mourning does not take effect on him,
is he not troubled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty of step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since there is no formal אנינות, the יום הכיפורים case is irrelevant to the decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: His emotional distress is enough to make the cases comparable, even without formal אנינות.

steps.title: משנה: the כהן גדול practices the daily service for seven days
steps.stepSummary: During the seven days of separation before יום הכיפורים, the כהן גדול personally does the main parts of the daily service.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: All seven days he sprinkles the blood, burns the קטורת, cleans the lamps, and offers the head and the leg.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the services the כהן גדול performs himself during the seven days before יום הכיפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal is training. By doing these parts of the daily תמיד service himself, he gets used to the work he will do alone on יום הכיפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkles / throws the blood on the מזבח
Cleans and prepares the מנורה lamps
The head and hind leg of the תמיד

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים הוּא זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם,
phrases.english: All seven days he sprinkles the blood,
and burns the incense,
and prepares the lamps,
and offers the head and the leg.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל שִׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים הוּא זוֹרֵק אֶת הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה; a new topic begins
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול personally performs the main daily services during the seven days of separation.

steps.title: משנה: all year the כהן גדול may take his pick
steps.stepSummary: On all other days, the כהן גדול may offer whatever he wants, because he has first choice both in offering and in taking portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: On all other days, if he wants to offer, he offers, because the כהן גדול offers a portion first and takes a portion first.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It explains the כהן גדול's rights during the rest of the year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the seven days he must serve, for practice. During the rest of the year it is his choice. As the most senior כהן, he has priority to perform any service he wants and to take any share of the offerings he wants.
steps.whatToRemember: Before יום הכיפורים, the כהן גדול must practice the service. All year he has the right of first choice.

phrases.english: And on all the other days,
if he wishes to offer — he offers,
for the High Priest offers a portion first,
and takes a portion first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁאָר כׇּל הַיָּמִים אִם רָצָה לְהַקְרִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Year-round, the כהן גדול may choose to offer, and he has first choice of portions.

steps.title: Who is the author of this משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's view this משנה follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who taught [this משנה]?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by asking whose opinion the משנה follows. This is a setup question for the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא suspects that the משנה's assumption, that the כהן גדול can serve during the seven days, does not fit every opinion. Identifying the author will show which view it matches.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא who taught this?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Who taught it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion the משנה follows

steps.title: רב חסדא: not like רבי עקיבא, because the sprinkling would make him impure
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא. According to רבי עקיבא, sprinkling פרה אדומה water on a pure person makes him impure, so the כהן גדול could not serve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is not like רבי עקיבא. For if it were רבי עקיבא, he said that a pure person on whom sprinkling fell is made impure by it. So how could he do the עבודה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא, because by רבי עקיבא's rule the כהן גדול would become impure during the seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the seven days, the כהן גדול is sprinkled with מי חטאת in case he became impure from a dead body. But רבי עקיבא holds that if a person was actually pure, the sprinkling itself makes him impure. Since the כהן גדול might be pure, the sprinkling could make him impure, and then he could not serve as the משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in accordance with רבי עקיבא
Sprinkling of מי חטאת (פרה אדומה water)

steps.confusionAlert: Normally the sprinkling makes an impure person pure. רבי עקיבא's surprising point is that the same sprinkling makes an already pure person impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a discussion of רבי עקיבא's rule and of when the כהן גדול is sprinkled, which the גמרא will develop next.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva.
For if it were Rabbi Akiva, didn't he say:
A pure person on whom sprinkling fell, it made him impure;
how can he perform the service!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא, since by his view the sprinkled כהן גדול might be impure and unable to serve.

steps.title: The Source: רבי עקיבא Says Sprinkling Makes a Pure Person Impure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי עקיבא holds sprinkling on the impure purifies, but sprinkling on the pure makes impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: "And the pure one shall sprinkle upon the impure one." On the impure, the sprinkling makes him pure. On the pure, it makes him impure. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב חסדא's claim about רבי עקיבא. A ברייתא quotes רבי עקיבא saying that sprinkling on a pure person makes him impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא reads the words "on the impure" as a limit. The water helps only an impure person, and it harms a pure one. That is why, according to him, the כהן גדול who is sprinkled during his seven days of separation could become impure and be unable to serve.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
"And the pure one shall sprinkle upon the impure one."
On the impure — he becomes pure,
but on the pure — he becomes impure,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for רב חסדא's description of רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that, according to רבי עקיבא, sprinkling on a pure person makes him impure.

steps.title: The חכמים: The Verse Is About Things That Can Become Impure
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the verse only teaches that sprinkling counts when it lands on something that can become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: these words were said only about things that can become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a different reading of the same verse in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, "on the impure" does not mean "not on the pure." It means the sprinkling must land on something that can receive טומאה at all, such as a person and not a living animal. So according to the חכמים, a pure person who is sprinkled stays pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that are able to become impure

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
These words are not stated
except regarding things that can receive impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reading of the same verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling counts only on something that can become impure. A pure person who is sprinkled is not made impure.

steps.title: What Does the חכמים' Rule Mean in Practice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference the חכמים' statement makes.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this rule about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a real case that shows the חכמים' rule. This question sets up the next step, where a משנה is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "things that can become impure" is abstract. The גמרא wants to know where it actually changes the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? / What case is this about?

phrases.english: What is this about?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical meaning of the חכמים' statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical case shows the rule that sprinkling counts only on things that can become impure?

steps.title: The משנה of Sprinkling on an Animal or a Person
steps.stepSummary: Water that lands on a person may be used again from the אזוב. Water that lands on an animal may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Someone meant to sprinkle on an animal but sprinkled on a person instead. If water is left on the אזוב, he should sprinkle again. Someone meant to sprinkle on a person but sprinkled on an animal instead. Even if water is left on the אזוב, he should not sprinkle again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a משנה that shows the חכמים' rule in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can become impure, so sprinkling on him counts as real sprinkling, and the leftover water stays usable. A living animal cannot become impure, so sprinkling on it is not real sprinkling. That misuse ruins the water left on the אזוב. The difference between the two cases is whether the thing sprinkled on can receive טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Hyssop, the plant dipped into the water to sprinkle

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Landing on the person (who can become impure) is the case where he may repeat. Landing on the animal (which cannot become impure) is the case where he may not repeat. His intention is not what decides it.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If he intended to sprinkle on an animal
but sprinkled on a person,
if water remains on the hyssop, he should repeat.
If he intended to sprinkle on a person
but sprinkled on an animal,
even if water remains on the hyssop, he should not repeat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sprinkling on something that cannot become impure (a living animal) is not real sprinkling, and it disqualifies the leftover water.

steps.title: What Is רבי עקיבא's Reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא learns his view from the verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source of רבי עקיבא's view. This question sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could be read the way the חכמים read it. So the גמרא wants to know what in the wording pushes רבי עקיבא to his reading.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Akiva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי עקיבא's view to find its source in the verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The textual basis for רבי עקיבא's view.

steps.title: The Extra Words "On the Impure"
steps.stepSummary: The Torah could have written "on him." Writing "on the impure" teaches that only the impure become pure, and the pure become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah could have written, "And the pure one shall sprinkle on him." Why does it say "on the impure"? Learn from this: on the impure, the sprinkling makes him pure. On the pure, it makes him impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא learns his view from words in the verse that seem extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The impure person was already mentioned, so "on him" would have been enough. Since the Torah spelled out "on the impure," רבי עקיבא learns a contrast from it: the water purifies the impure but makes the pure impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah (the Merciful One) write

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write:
"And the pure one shall sprinkle on him";
why does it say "on the impure"?
Learn from it: on the impure, he becomes pure,
but on the pure, he becomes impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about רבי עקיבא's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words "on the impure" teach a contrast: the water purifies the impure and makes the pure impure.

steps.title: The חכמים' Use of the Words and Their קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use the extra words to teach the rule about things that can become impure. They prove with a קל וחומר that a pure person stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? These words come to teach about things that can become impure. But here, there is a קל וחומר: if the water makes an impure person pure, then surely it does not make a pure person impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the חכמים deal with the extra words, and gives their logical argument against רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use the extra words for a different lesson: sprinkling must be on something that can become impure. They also argue with logic. Something strong enough to take away טומאה should certainly not create טומאה in a person who is already pure.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger one (a fortiori)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis:
this is about things that can receive impurity,
that is what it comes to teach.
But here, it is a kal vachomer:
if on the impure, he becomes pure,
then on the pure, all the more so he stays pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the חכמים' use of the same words and gives a logical argument against רבי עקיבא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra words teach the rule about things that can become impure. A קל וחומר shows that a pure person stays pure.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: This Law Is Beyond Logic
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the קל וחומר. He says this law is the very puzzle that even שלמה המלך could not understand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? This is what שלמה said: "I said, I will become wise, but it is far from me."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא answers the קל וחומר. He answers that this law is not meant to follow logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water that purifies the impure but makes the pure impure is a contradiction. That contradiction is exactly what שלמה could not understand. Since the law is above human reason, a קל וחומר cannot overturn it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, how does he answer?
This is what Solomon said:
"I said, I will become wise,
but it is far from me."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי עקיבא against the חכמים' קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects logical reasoning for a law that is above logic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר proves that a pure person cannot become impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The laws of פרה אדומה are beyond reason, so a קל וחומר does not apply to them.

steps.title: The חכמים: שלמה's Puzzle Was the מזה vs. the נוגע
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say שלמה's puzzle was a different law. The one who sprinkles and the one sprinkled on are pure, but one who touches the water is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים? That verse is about this: the one who sprinkles and the one sprinkled on are pure, while one who touches the water is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the חכמים also accept שלמה's puzzle, but they apply it to a different law of פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים agree that the laws of פרה אדומה contain a mystery. For them, the mystery is that the sprinkler and the person sprinkled on stay pure, yet someone who simply touches the water becomes impure. So the verse is not a source for רבי עקיבא's rule, and the חכמים' קל וחומר still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: sprinkling מי חטאת on a pure person makes him impure. That is why our משנה about the כהן גדול does not follow him. The חכמים: a pure person stays pure, proven by a קל וחומר. Both sides agree that פרה אדומה holds a mystery that שלמה could not grasp. They disagree about what that mystery is.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, how do they explain that verse?
That verse is about how the sprinkler and the one sprinkled on are pure,
but one who touches the water is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the חכמים explain שלמה's verse without accepting רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלמה's verse supports רבי עקיבא's paradox.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמה's verse refers to the sprinkler and the one sprinkled on staying pure while one who touches the water becomes impure.

steps.title: Challenge: The Torah says the sprinkler must wash his clothes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the מזה is pure. A פסוק says he must wash his clothes, which shows he became impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the one who sprinkles really pure? But it is written: 'And the one who sprinkles the purification water shall wash his clothes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what the חכמים said in Step 18, that the one who sprinkles (מזה) is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the Torah, washing clothes (כיבוס בגדים) is a sign that someone became impure. If the Torah tells the מזה to wash his clothes, he cannot be pure.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who sprinkles the פרה אדומה water
The purification water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
He shall wash his clothes, a sign of impurity

phrases.english: And is the one who sprinkles pure?
But isn't it written: 'And the one who sprinkles the purification water'
'shall wash his clothes'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the חכמים's claim in Step 18 that the מזה is pure
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's statement that the one who sprinkles is pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק requires the מזה to wash his clothes, and that only happens to someone who is impure

steps.title: Answer: 'Sprinkler' here means one who touches
steps.stepSummary: The first attempted answer: in this פסוק the word 'מזה' really means the one who touches the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one who sprinkles' mean here? One who touches.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the חכמים by reading the word 'מזה' in the פסוק as 'נוגע', one who touches the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'מזה' means a person who touches the water, then the actual sprinkler is never mentioned as impure. That would leave the חכמים's rule in place.

phrases.english: What is 'one who sprinkles'?
One who touches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19 by reinterpreting a word
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק speaks of the actual sprinkler
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מזה' in the פסוק means one who touches the water

steps.title: Challenge: The verse already mentions the toucher separately
steps.stepSummary: The 'touches' reading is rejected for two reasons. The same פסוק names the נוגע separately, and the two get different laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says 'one who sprinkles', and it also separately says 'one who touches'! And besides, the one who sprinkles needs to wash his clothes, while the one who touches does not need to wash his clothes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer of Step 20 with two strong proofs from the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the פסוק writes both 'מזה' and 'נוגע', so they cannot be the same person. Second, the פסוק gives the מזה washing of clothes but not the נוגע, so they have different laws.

phrases.english: But isn't it written 'one who sprinkles',
and isn't 'one who touches' also written?
phrases.notes: Both appear in the same פסוק, so they must be different people

phrases.english: And furthermore: the sprinkler requires washing of clothes,
while the toucher does not require washing of clothes!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 20
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק names both separately and gives them different laws

steps.title: New answer: 'Sprinkler' means one who carries the water
steps.stepSummary: A new answer: the 'מזה' in the פסוק is someone who carries the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'one who sprinkles' mean? One who carries.
steps.whatsHappening: With 'אלא', the גמרא drops the first answer and gives a new one. The 'מזה' who washes his clothes is really a נושא, one who carries the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying causes a stronger impurity than touching, so washing clothes fits a carrier. Now the actual sprinkler can still be pure, as the חכמים said.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which drops the earlier answer

phrases.english: Rather: what is 'one who sprinkles'?
One who carries.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer with a new reading
steps.terutzMaskana: 'מזה' means one who carries, so washing clothes fits and the real sprinkler stays pure

steps.title: Challenge: Then why not just write 'carrier'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Torah used the word 'sprinkles' if it meant 'carries'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the Merciful One write 'one who carries'. Why does it write 'one who sprinkles'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If the Torah meant a carrier, it should have said so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not use a strange word for no reason. Using 'מזה' to mean 'נושא' needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

phrases.english: Then let the Merciful One write 'one who carries'!
What is the reason 'one who sprinkles' is written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording behind the answer of Step 22
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the meaning is 'carrier', the word 'sprinkler' seems to be the wrong word

steps.title: Answer: The word teaches the carrier needs enough for a sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מזה' teaches that a carrier only becomes impure if he carries a sprinkling's worth of water (שיעור הזאה).
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that we require the amount of a sprinkling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the odd word. It tells us how much water a carrier must carry to become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the carrier a 'sprinkler' links his carrying to sprinkling. So he becomes impure only if he carries enough water to sprinkle with.

keyTerms.meaning: The minimum amount needed for a sprinkling

steps.whyThisMatters: This creates a practical minimum amount for the impurity of carrying מי חטאת.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that we require the measure of sprinkling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: The unusual word adds a law
steps.terutzMaskana: The word teaches that a carrier must carry a שיעור הזאה to become impure

steps.title: Challenge: What about the view that sprinkling has no minimum?
steps.stepSummary: This answer works for the view that sprinkling needs a minimum amount. For the view that it needs no minimum, there is no such amount to learn.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says sprinkling requires a minimum amount. But for the one who says sprinkling does not require a minimum amount, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 24 based on a known מחלוקת about whether sprinkling has a minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a sprinkling needs no minimum amount, then a 'sprinkling's worth' means nothing. So the word 'מזה' would teach nothing for that view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who said:
sprinkling requires a minimum measure.
But according to the one who said:
sprinkling does not require a minimum measure,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the answer of Step 24 against an opposing view
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'מזה' teaches a שיעור הזאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For the view that sprinkling has no minimum, there is no שיעור to learn

steps.title: Answer: No minimum on the person, but a minimum in the vessel
steps.stepSummary: Even that view only means that any amount may land on the person. The vessel used for dipping must still hold a minimum amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says sprinkling does not require a minimum amount, that applies only on the man's back. But in the vessel, a minimum amount is required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by splitting the case into two places: water on the person's body, and water in the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'no minimum' view is only about how much water must land on the impure man. Everyone agrees the vessel must hold a set amount, and that is the שיעור the carrier needs.

keyTerms.meaning: On the back (body) of the man

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two amounts. The person can get even a drop. The vessel must hold enough for dipping.

phrases.english: Even according to the one who said
sprinkling does not require a minimum measure,
that applies only on the back of the man,
but in the vessel, it requires a measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 25 by limiting the 'no minimum' view
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case (person compared with vessel)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'no minimum' view means there is no minimum at all
steps.terutzMaskana: No minimum is needed on the person, but the vessel needs one, and that is the carrier's שיעור

steps.title: Proof from a משנה: How much water the vessel must hold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה that sets the amount of water a vessel must hold for sprinkling. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: How much water should be in them so that it is enough for sprinkling? Enough to dip...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove that the vessel needs a minimum amount of water. The quote is cut off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה asks 'how much' and gives an amount. That proves the vessel has a set minimum, even for those who need no minimum on the person.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'מזה' who washes his clothes is really the carrier. He becomes impure only when carrying a sprinkling's worth of water, which is measured by how much the vessel must hold.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
How much should be in them
so that it will be enough for sprinkling?
Enough that one can dip
phrases.notes: The quote continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the claim in Step 26
steps.raayaObject: That the vessel used for sprinkling must hold a minimum amount of water
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (פרה 12:5) giving the amount needed in the vessel
